newsitem.title: UK: UK's GEC in MoU on Thomson-CSF privatisation.
newsitem.headline: UK's GEC in MoU on Thomson-CSF privatisation.

text.p: Britain's General Electric Company Plc said on Wednesday it had signed an agreement with Alcatel-Dassault and the Lagardere Group, the two candidates vying to buy state-owned Thomson-CSF from the French government, which could eventually lead to a link-up between parts of Thomson and GEC after the privatisation.

Lagardere said earlier it had filed its final offer for French defence group Thomson-CSF, saying it had the necessary finances for the acquisition and an eventual public offer to buy out Thomson-CSF's minority shareholders if its bid succeeded.
French electronic engineering group Alcatel Alsthom said it made a joint bid with Dassault Industries and hoped that winner.

The French government is selling its 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF, after abandoning last year an attempt to sell parent company Thomson SA, which also owns consumer electronics group Thomson Multimedia.
According to the memorandum of understanding (MoU) GEC intends to hold talks with whichever of its partners is successful in gaining control of Thomson-CSF.
"In these discussions, full regard will be paid to the sovereignty of the British, French, Italian and United States governments, and others if appropriate," GEC said.
GEC-Marconi and Thomson-CSF are the two biggest defence electronics companies in Europe.

The French government had ruled out a full bid by the British company citing national security interests, but had said it would welcome it linking up with one of the main French bidders after the sale.
Meanwhile, British Aerospace Plc has been backing Lagardere's bid,with a view to absorbing Thomson's missile business into their own joint venture, Matra BAe Dynamics.
